observation_summary: The Regula Falsi solver fails with a TooManyEvaluationsException because it does not detect when the algorithm is stuck due to floating-point precision limitations, causing it to repeatedly evaluate the same point.
hypothesis: The Regula Falsi solver implementation in BaseSecantSolver lacks a convergence check for when the algorithm becomes stuck due to floating-point precision limitations. Specifically, when the calculated next approximation 'x' is identical to one of the existing bounds ('x1' or 'x0'), the algorithm fails to make progress, leading to an infinite loop until the evaluation limit is reached.
prediction: Adding a check to detect if 'x' equals 'x1' (or 'x0') and throwing a ConvergenceException will resolve the issue by terminating the loop gracefully when no further progress can be made.
experiment_rationale: The evidence shows the solver enters an infinite loop (or hits max evaluations) because the update formula fails to produce a new, distinct point. This is a classic case of missing a termination condition (a guard) for a specific algorithmic state.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a missing check for a degenerate state in the Regula Falsi algorithm. The implementation continues to iterate even when the update formula stops producing new values, which is a failure of the loop termination logic. This falls squarely under the 'Checking' category as it involves adding a validation check to prevent an invalid/stuck state.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the algorithm itself has limitations, the fix is specifically the addition of a guard condition to detect the stuck state, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
